Warehouse Manager

Factor_ a brand of HelloFresh is seeking a Warehouse Manager to support their Aurora, IL location.

Shift-Thursday to Sunday 4:30am to 3:30pm

You will ...

· Oversee the strategic operations within the functional areas of receiving, shipping, storage / distribution of goods, and logistics.

· Direct activities and provide coaching and guidance to associates, leads, and supervisors.

· Work alongside and with the team, providing guidance as needed to ensure maximum productivity.

· Work with senior Management to complete the given directives of the Company.

· Responsible for ensuring compliance with all safety, GMP and SQF policies/procedures, as well as adherence to PPE/hygiene policies.

· This managerial position is expected to cultivate a culture in line with Hello Fresh’s core values.

· Ensure a high level of internal and external customer service. Investigate (and correct) customer issues and complaints.

· Manages the department engaged in essential warehouse functions (receiving, shipping, and distribution) to ensure high productivity and high technical integrity.

· Performing internal audits.

· Coordinate objectives with production procedures in cooperation with other plant managers to maximize product reliability and minimize costs.

· Create and implement processes and procedures.

· Relay quality philosophy to all warehouse personnel.

· Maintain active role on internal continuous improvement teams.

· Design, develop and implement warehousing training programs based on quarterly performance reviews

· Interact with procurement to ensure adequate supply of all inventory and ingredients.

· Addressing nonconformities from previous internal and external audits.

· Conducting a management review of the warehouse essential functions.

· Following-up on and closing pending preventive and corrective action requests.

· Ensuring that documentation and design controls are appropriate for organization.

· Assisting the management team and provide support as necessary.

· Provide all employees with necessary tools, proper training and corrective direction.

You are...

· A Leader: train and develop a large group of employees

· Performance Manager of warehouse employees

· Problem Solver/Analytical

· Detailed Oriented and Results Driven

· Communicator: speak to employees with tact and diplomacy

· Time Manager: tracking/monitoring production and maintaining productivity

· Technical: computer literacy to input information into the computer

· Able to take direction and relay information to employees

At a minimum, you have...

· Associate’s degree or related management work experience.

· At least 5 years of work experience in warehouse management, should be combined with a demonstrated track-record of accomplishments as a manager, and with satisfying customers in technology-driven, developing companies.

This job description is intended to provide a general overview of the responsibilities. However, the Company reserves the right to adjust, modify, or reassign work tasks and responsibilities as needed to meet changing business needs, operational requirements, or other factors.

Hey there!

We’re Fever , the world’s leading tech platform for culture and live entertainment.

Our mission? To democratize access to culture and entertainment. With our proprietary cutting-edge technology and data-driven approach, we’re revolutionizing the way people engage with live entertainment.

Every month, our platform inspires over 300 million people in +55 countries (and counting) to discover unforgettable experiences while also empowering event creators with our data and technology, helping them scale, innovate, and enhance their events to reach new audiences.

Our results? We’ve teamed up with major industry leaders like Netflix, F.C. Barcelona, and Primavera Sound, presented international award-winning experiences, and are backed by several leading global investors! Impressive, right?

To achieve our mission, we are looking for bar-raisers with a hands-on mindset who are eager to help shape the future of entertainment!

Ready to be part of the experience?

Now, let’s discuss this role and what you will do to help achieve Fever’s mission.

You will be responsible for the physical operations of merchandise within our facility, ensuring that every item is where it needs to be, when it needs to be there.

We are seeking a highly organized and strategic Warehouse Manager to oversee our logistics hub and drive operational excellence. In this role, you will lead daily warehouse activities, optimize inventory control through ODOO, manage budgets, and ensure seamless coordination with internal teams and external vendors.

· Team Leadership: Lead and direct the warehouse operations staff to ensure high performance, safety, and alignment with company goals.

· Operational Excellence: Enforce and optimize Fever’s internal operational processes to maintain high standards of efficiency and quality.

· Logistics & Shipment Management: Oversee all inbound and outbound logistics, ensuring the timely, accurate, and cost-effective handling of all freight.

· Inventory Control: Manage inventory integrity within ODOO ; oversee precise categorization, execute regular audits, and dynamically update stock levels based on receiving and shipping workflows.

· Performance Metrics: Define, track, and report on Key Performance Indicators (KPIs) related to inventory accuracy, facility throughput, and operational efficiency.

· Financial & Budgetary Oversight: Develop and manage budgets for workforce allocation, logistics functions, and facility support costs (including safety, security, insurance, and maintenance).

· Cross-Functional Financial Support: Partner with the Finance team to meticulously track and allocate operational costs per Intellectual Property (IP) based on real-time warehouse utilization.

· Safety & Compliance: Guarantee full compliance with occupational health and safety regulations; design and execute a comprehensive Facility Maintenance Plan to sustain a hazard-free work environment.

· Stakeholder Management: Serve as the primary Point of Contact (POC) for key internal and external stakeholders (e.g., F.O., N.V.) regarding their stored inventory and logistics needs.

· Vendor & Agency Relations: Cultivate and manage strategic business relationships with staffing agencies for flexible labor solutions and logistics vendors for shipping optimization.

· Continuous Improvement: Standardize warehouse workflows and implement scalability strategies to support Fever's rapid growth.

· Experience: 3+ years of experienc in a warehouse or logistics operations and environment, specifically with picking, packing, and reception.

· English : good written and verbal English communication skills, enabling seamless collaboration with global teams.

· Inventory management experience and skills.

· Technical Skills: Comfortable using google sheets and excel files, as well as digital tools such as PDAs and Warehouse Management Systems (SGA).

· Certifications: A valid forklift operator license (Carné de Carretillero) and heavy equipment certified is highly valued.

· Strong leadership skills : confortable collaborating with cross-functional teams and building strong relationships with the business units we support. Experience in managing unique and complex situations in a fast-paced, high-pressure environment is necessary.

· Detail-Oriented: Focus on accuracy to prevent inventory discrepancies and shipping errors.

· Physical Stamina: Ability to handle the physical demands of a warehouse role, including moving merchandise and standing for extended periods.

· Location: Ability to commute to Logistic Park San Agustín, San Agustín del Guadalix.

About Role
We are building a supply-chain organization capable of supporting our transition from laboratory-scale development to factory-scale operations. We are looking for an Inventory Manager to build and operate our inventory function from the ground up.
This is a highly hands-on role. In the near term, you may start with an empty room and be responsible for determininga what racks, shelving, bins, labels, scanners, workflows, and systems are needed to turn it into a functional stockroom. You will receive material, organize inventory, perform counts, move parts between buildings, resolve discrepancies, and establish the processes others will eventually follow.
As we grow, you will have the opportunity to develop this foundation into a full-scale, multi-site factory inventory operation. You may hire and manage contractors or onsite inventory administrators, but this role will initially have a significant individual-contributor component and will remain accountable for day-to-day execution.
This role owns inventory and internal logistics. It does not own purchasing, production planning, or inbound and outbound supplier logistics.
This role is based in San Francisco, CA and requires in-person presence 5 days a week.

Build inventory operations from the ground up across various OpenAI facilities.
Design and set up stockrooms, receiving areas, and material-storage locations, including selecting racks, shelving, bins, carts, labeling equipment, scanners, and other infrastructure.
Personally execute core inventory activities, including receiving, labeling, putaway, picking, kitting, issuing, cycle counting, transfers, returns, and inventory adjustments.
Establish practical receiving procedures that ensure incoming material is identified, recorded, inspected or quarantined when appropriate, and made available quickly.
Hire, train, and manage contractors or onsite inventory administrators as volume and facility needs grow.
Create location structures, naming conventions, barcode workflows, material-status controls, and standard work.
Maintain accurate visibility into what inventory exists, where it is located, and whether it is available for use.
Establish and maintain cycle-counting and physical-inventory programs, investigate discrepancies, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions.
Own internal logistics and material movement between company facilities, including transfer processes, delivery schedules, chain of custody, transaction accuracy, and reconciliation.
Develop appropriate controls for serialized, lot-controlled, high-value, consigned, returned, obsolete, and nonconforming material.
Serve as the business owner for inventory tools and workflows.
Partner with the systems team to translate operational needs into requirements, prioritize improvements, test new functionality, and drive adoption.
Create procedures and training that allow inventory operations to be replicated consistently at new facilities.
Identify inventory risks, shortages, excess material, unidentified material, and process breakdowns before they disrupt operations.

s.h: You might thrive in this role if you
s.t:
4+ years of experience in inventory management, warehouse operations, materials operations, internal logistics, or a related field.
Experience building or substantially improving an inventory operation, not only working within an established one.
Strong working knowledge of receiving, putaway, picking, kitting, cycle counting, material transfers, inventory reconciliation, and physical inventory controls.
Willingness to work directly in stockrooms, receiving areas, laboratories, and manufacturing spaces.
Ability to move comfortably between strategic design and hands-on execution.
Experience selecting and implementing physical inventory infrastructure such as racks, shelving, bins, labeling systems, barcode scanners, and material-handling equipment.
Familiarity with ERP, WMS, MES, or inventory-management systems and the transactions required to maintain accurate inventory.
Willingness to travel regularly among company facilities.

s.h: Within the first 6 months, you will have
s.t:
Turned empty or informal storage areas into organized, functional stockrooms.
Established consistent receiving, storage, counting, and material-transfer processes across active facilities.
Created reliable visibility into what inventory exists, where it is located, and whether it is available for use.
Implemented practical location controls, labeling standards, transaction procedures, and cycle counting.
Built a reliable inter-building logistics process with clear ownership and traceability.

Factor Canada is seeking a Warehouse Supervisor to join our team at our Distribution Centre. Reporting to the Warehouse Manager, you will lead a team of warehouse associates and leads to ensure seamless day-to-day operations.

Your focus will be to ensure that all direct and indirect material inventory movements, quantities, and quality are tracked accurately at all times. If you are a hands-on operator who thrives on detail and organization, obsesses over delivering measurable results, and has a passion for food, this is the perfect opportunity for you!

s.h: Lettuce share what this role will be responsible for
s.t:
Supervise Warehouse Operations: Direct and oversee warehouse staff in receiving, shipping, and storing goods, ensuring that all SOPs and safety regulations are followed.
Manage Inventory Accuracy: Ensure real-time, accurate inventory records through cycle counts, stock transfers, and inventory reconciliations, addressing discrepancies with root cause analysis.
Train Warehouse Staff: Provide training to warehouse personnel on inventory procedures, safety regulations, and systems to maintain high standards of efficiency and accuracy.
Coordinate Inventory Movements: Organize the movement of materials within the warehouse and coordinate inventory transfers with other departments like Planning, Production, and Supply Chain.
Enforce Safety Compliance: Ensure compliance with OH&S acts and warehouse safety regulations, and report hazards or dangers.
Support Cross-functional Collaboration: Liaise with other departments such as Finance, Operations, and Quality to solve problems, enhance inventory metrics, and streamline operations.
Monitor Warehouse Performance: Measure and report the effectiveness of warehousing activities, including employee performance, to improve operational efficiency.
Optimize Storage and Space Utilization: Organize and maintain inventory storage areas, adhering to storage design principles, and recommend improvements for efficient space utilization.
Lead Process Improvements: Support and lead system implementations and warehouse projects to improve overall workflow and inventory accuracy.
Investigate Discrepancies: Conduct thorough investigations into inventory variances and implement corrective actions to prevent recurrence.
Schedule and Coordinate Material Handling: Plan and execute the movement of materials in and out of the warehouse, coordinating closely with other departments to meet operational needs.
Document and Update Records: Maintain accurate data entry in inventory systems (e.g., Microsoft Office, Google Sheets), and ensure all transactions and physical counts are reconciled properly.

s.h: Sound a-peeling? Here's what we're looking for
s.t:
4+ years inventory, warehousing, manufacturing and/or supply chain experience with a Bachelor’s in Engineering, Business or a related field
Strong analytical, problem solving, and Excel skills
Energy, enthusiasm, and a can-do attitude. Used to working in a high pressure, fast paced, and constantly changing environment
Drive and self-motivation. We seek a potential leader who competes to win and have the burning desire to make a meaningful difference in our business and lives of our employees
An effective collaborator, who empowers and enables others to share ideas, raises awareness, gets buy-in, and delivers fast and well-rounded solutions to complex problems
Ability to handle multiple projects and assignments able to prioritize and meet budgets deadlines and achieve objectives;
Ability to maintain sensitive and confidential information
Professional certifications and/or licenses with Lean Six Sigma preferred
Availability to work weekend schedules and cold facilities
Experience with Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint), Google Suite (Calendar, Gmail, Docs, Sheets), and video conferencing (Hangouts Meet)

The Inventory Manager oversees stock levels and inventory health within the warehouse from initial reception through to customer dispatch or vendor return . Reporting directly to the Warehouse Manager , this role leads a team of Inventory Supervisors to enforce FIFO models, execute cycle counts, optimize space utilization, and maintain inventory accuracy to support seamless e-commerce fulfillment .

Inventory & Cycle Count Ownership: Own end-to-end stock control and lead daily/monthly cycle counts, maintaining accurate records of all stock received, moved, and shipped out.
Commercial Alignment & Aging Stock: Partner with commercial teams to address aging inventory through return-to-vendor (RTV) actions or promotional sales campaigns.
Space Utilization & Process Mapping: Optimize warehouse storage capacity and map inventory processes against Jumia best practices, ensuring strict FIFO execution and safe item handling.
Reporting & Compliance: Prepare detailed operational reports on stock levels, adjustments, and storage compliance while ensuring full system adherence.
Team Leadership & Collaboration: Supervise and develop Inventory Supervisors while working cross-functionally with Inbound, Outbound, and Aftersales teams.

Education & Certifications: Bachelor’s degree in Business Administration, Logistics, Supply Chain, or a related field. Project management certifications and basic finance knowledge are added advantages.
Professional Experience: Minimum 4 years of warehouse management or FMCG experience, with deep knowledge of direct-to-consumer e-commerce fulfillment, inventory software, and forecasting.
Language & Technical Skills: Advanced Microsoft Excel skills and fluency in English, French, and/or Arabic (based on location).
Core Competencies: Exceptional data analysis, organizational, and creative problem-solving skills with a focus on high detail and independent follow-through in fast-paced environments.

The Inventory Manager is responsible for maintaining inventory accuracy, stock integrity, and optimal space utilization across all fulfillment centers. This position acts as the primary guardian of physical stock, ensuring total alignment between system records and physical quantities while minimizing stock loss, aging, and discrepancies.
What You Will Be Doing
Execute inventory audit programs: Design and execute daily cycle count programs, wall-to-wall stock counts, and periodic inventory audits across all warehouse locations.
Investigate stock variances: Analyze root causes of inventory discrepancies, stock losses, and shrinkage, implementing preventative corrective action plans.
Stock aging & capacity planning: Oversee inventory aging management, product slotting, putaway strategies, and storage capacity optimization.
Inventory disposition: Partner with Commercial, Inbound, and Outbound teams to manage slow-moving, expired, or damaged inventory disposal and liquidation processes.
Process compliance: Ensure strict adherence to Warehouse Management System (WMS) processes, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and internal audit guidelines.

Education: Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Logistics, Industrial Engineering, or Finance.
Experience: 4+ years of inventory control and warehouse management experience within e-commerce, retail, or FMCG.
Technical Proficiency: High proficiency in Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), ERP tools, and data analytics (Excel, SQL is a plus).
Track Record: Proven track record of maintaining high inventory accuracy (>99%) and managing shrinkage controls.
Core Competencies: Strong analytical mindset, high attention to detail, and team management capabilities.
